questions.reason: The captured Rate Limits page states verbatim: "Error messages can vary by the limit reached; use the HTTP status and header for retry handling rather than matching the message text." That establishes option b, and the page's own 429 example carrying `Retry-After: 60` plus the note that keyless access "uses a different error format and separate limits" rule out c and d.

Under "Rotating your API keys" the page says "As a general security best practice, we recommend rotating your API keys periodically (e.g., every 90 days)", which supports the 90-day answer; the leak-response steps are a separate section, so the leak-only and rotate-once options are unsupported.

The capability table reads "**Map** | You need a site's structure before crawling it.", exactly the stem's need; the Search, Crawl and Research rows in the same table cover different criteria (unknown sources, reading many pages, cited synthesis), so only Map fits.

The Credits & Pricing page gives "**Regular Mapping:** Every 10 successful pages returned cost **1 API credit**" against "**Map with (`instructions`):** Every 10 successful pages returned cost **2 API credits**", which is precisely the doubling the correct option states; Crawl's "Mapping Cost + Extraction Cost" formula is documented for Crawl only and the page never ties instructions to extract_depth.

The MCP guide's API key selection note says "**Team account**: If your team has a key named `mcp_auth_default`, it will be used for all OAuth-authenticated requests." The personal-priority bullet applies only when "both your personal account and your team have a key named `mcp_auth_default`", and the `default`/first-available fallbacks only when "no `mcp_auth_default` key exists", neither of which holds in the stem.

The Usage reference describes key.search_usage as "Search endpoint credits used for this API key during the current billing cycle", while key.usage is "Total credits used for this API key" and account.search_usage is "Search endpoint credits used for this plan" - so only the keyed, Search-specific field answers the stem.

The Extract reference's 400 response reads "Bad Request. More than 20 URLs, an empty URL list, or no URLs passing validation are rejected. When all URLs fail validation, detail.failed_results describes the individual failures.", and the allInvalidUrls example shows per-URL entries inside detail, which refutes the generic-error, one-at-a-time and results-array options.

The Crawl reference defines select_paths as "Regex patterns to select only URLs with specific path patterns (e.g., `/docs/.*`, `/api/v1.*`)" and exclude_paths as "Regex patterns to exclude URLs with specific path patterns (e.g., `/private/.*`, `/admin/.*`)"; select_domains/exclude_domains match "domains or subdomains", max_depth bounds distance from the base URL, allow_external covers external-domain links and limit caps total links, so none of those scope a path.
